title: PE content with a document or image filename
description: Admits complete HTTP 200 response files with a selected document or image filename, checks bounded PE headers and emits a Notice only after HTTP and file completion agree with Content-Length.

topics.title: Load HTTP Notice and PE helpers
topics.description: The HTTP scripts provide transaction and file association state. The Notice framework supplies NOTICE. The relative pe load supplies structural PE checks and loads filename selection and shared limits.

topics.title: Declare the finding type
topics.description: DocumentImageMismatch is added to Notice::Type inside the PEFileDisguise export block. finish selects this type after the filename, structure and completion checks.

topics.title: Count active context ownership
topics.description: Health tracks active_contexts and peak_active_contexts. Admission increments active ownership, release_context decrements it once, and the peak records the highest simultaneous count.
links: Use the active count for admission

topics.title: Count retained prefix bytes
topics.description: retained_prefix_bytes measures the aggregate bytes still held in context prefixes. prefix_data increments it as bytes are copied; release_prefix subtracts the current string length. The peak records the highest retained total.

topics.title: Count admissions drops and notices
topics.description: eligible_files counts admitted contexts, admission_drops counts attempts declined at the context cap, and notices counts emitted findings. The exported health record initializes each metric to zero.

topics.title: Keep transaction and file identity
topics.description: Context stores the connection UID and conn_id, the file FUID and the HTTP transaction depth. Admission captures these values so later completion can verify the transaction and the Notice can identify both endpoints and file.

topics.title: Keep selected name and declared length
topics.description: filename contains the Content-Disposition selection and declared contains the checked Content-Length. They are copied into shared context at admission and used for completion equality and Notice evidence.
links: Copy the header selection into context
Trace name and declared bytes in the Notice

topics.title: Keep bounded parse progress
topics.description: prefix retains only the staged header bytes. parsed starts F, format starts empty and bad starts F. Prefix classification sets parsed and format, while any quality failure can set bad.

topics.title: Separate completion from release
topics.description: http_done and file_done start F and record their independent native completions. released starts F and becomes a tombstone when budgets are released, keeping late callbacks from reusing the context.

topics.title: Keep final native file counts
topics.description: seen and total start zero and are filled from native file state at removal. completion_ok compares both against the stored declared length.

links.label: Compare observed total and declared bytes

topics.title: Track response header quality and multiplicity
topics.description: Headers begins with bad=F and zero counts for Content-Disposition, Content-Length, Content-Encoding and Content-Type. The header handler marks conflicting framing or repeated selected headers as bad.
links: Reject duplicate disposition or length headers

topics.title: Keep response selection and file count
topics.description: Header state holds the selected filename, the declared length and the number of associated response files. Empty initial values keep admission closed until accepted metadata and exactly one file are present.
links: Use the header selection and counts

topics.title: Attach header and context state to HTTP
topics.description: Each HTTP::Info has default fresh Headers and an optional Context reference. The reference is shared with the admitted native file so both completion callbacks update the same object.
links: Share one context between HTTP and file callbacks

topics.title: Attach the shared context and declare its byte callback
topics.description: fa_file gains an optional pfd_context. prefix_data is declared with the exact file and byte string event signature used in the DATA_EVENT analyzer arguments.

ranges.code:
redef record fa_file += { pfd_context: Context &optional; };
global prefix_data: event(f: fa_file, data: string);

links: Attach the exact prefix callback instance

topics.title: Detach this exact prefix callback instance
topics.description: stop_prefix calls Files::remove_analyzer with f, Files::ANALYZER_DATA_EVENT and [$stream_event=prefix_data]. Those arguments identify this policy callback instance; DATA_EVENT instances with other arguments remain attached. Queued callbacks still test the shared state before collecting bytes.

topics.title: Release the retained string and its byte budget
topics.description: release_prefix subtracts the current prefix length from health$retained_prefix_bytes and replaces the prefix with an empty string. Classification can release bytes while keeping context ownership for completion.
links: Release bytes during final context cleanup

topics.title: Release a context at most once
topics.description: release_context returns immediately when released is already T. This guard protects the byte budget and active context count when rejection and late completion paths meet.

topics.title: Clear prefix ownership and tombstone the context
topics.description: release_prefix clears retained bytes, released becomes T and active_contexts decreases once. The shared reference remains reachable by queued callbacks, which observe the tombstone.
links: Clear the prefix string and byte count

topics.title: Mark a context bad and release it
topics.description: reject_context sets bad=T and calls release_context immediately. Quality, framing and parser failures all converge here to release owned budgets.

topics.title: Ignore completion on released context
topics.description: finish returns when the shared context is already released. A later HTTP or file callback therefore cannot emit another Notice or release the budgets again.

topics.title: Release a failed completion context
topics.description: A bad context calls reject_context and returns. This path can clean up a quality failure before both completion flags become true.
links: Mark and release the failed context

topics.title: Wait for both native completion gates
topics.description: For a context still eligible for a finding, finish returns until both http_done and file_done are T. Header classification alone and either single completion callback keep the Notice path closed.
links: Set the native file completion gate

topics.title: Combine exact completion and accepted format
topics.description: completion_ok receives both flags, bad, seen, total and declared from the shared context. Its T result must coincide with a nonempty x$format to enter the Notice block.

links.label: Follow the actual completion predicate definition

links: See where the format is stored

topics.title: Emit the exact type and reason
topics.description: NOTICE uses DocumentImageMismatch and the literal msg PE content advertised with a document or image filename. The preceding gates establish the filename selection, supported PE structure and complete body length agreement.

ranges.code:
NOTICE([$note=DocumentImageMismatch,
$msg="PE content advertised with a document or image filename",

topics.title: Define the ordered evidence template
topics.description: The fmt template records FUID, UID, filename bytes as hexadecimal, the literal filename source content-disposition, the PE format, observed and declared byte counts, and originator and responder ports in that order. The eight dynamic placeholders map to the arguments on the following source line.

topics.title: Supply each evidence placeholder in order
topics.description: The arguments are x$fuid, x$uid, bytestring_to_hexstr(x$filename), the PE32 or PE32+ conditional, x$seen, x$declared, x$id$orig_p and x$id$resp_p. Hex encoding retains the selected filename bytes in a printable field. seen comes from native file removal; declared comes from Content-Length.
links: Trace FUID UID filename declared length and connection ID

topics.title: Attach the client and server connection identity
topics.description: The Notice record copies uid, conn_id and fuid from the admitted context. src is the connection originator address, dst is the responder address and p is the responder port. The admitted bytes came from the HTTP responder, while these record fields retain connection client to server orientation.

topics.title: Render the accepted PE format
topics.description: The actual fmt argument x$format=="pe32" ? "PE32" : "PE32+" renders pe32 as PE32 and the accepted pe32plus path as PE32+. A nonempty format reaches this argument only after pe_format returned a supported pair.

topics.title: Count the emitted finding
topics.description: health$notices increments immediately after NOTICE executes, inside the final completion and format branch.

topics.title: Release context after the final decision
topics.description: Once both gates are present, finish releases the context whether the final predicate emitted a Notice or not. The release operation clears any remaining prefix budget and tombstones shared state.

topics.title: Require bounded decimal Content-Length syntax
topics.description: decimal_length strips surrounding whitespace, then requires a nonempty string of ASCII digits no longer than max_header_value_bytes. Invalid input returns zero, which the header handler marks bad.
links: Use zero as a rejected length

topics.title: Accumulate decimal digits from zero
topics.description: n starts zero and i visits each byte of the accepted digit string. The next operations convert one byte and check capacity before multiplying n by ten.

topics.title: Convert one ASCII digit byte
topics.description: octet(v,i)-48 converts the already validated ASCII digit to a value from zero through nine, then increments i.

topics.title: Check the object cap before multiplying
topics.description: n must be at most (max_object_bytes-digit)/10 before n=n*10+digit. A larger prefix returns zero, keeping the accumulated Content-Length within max_object_bytes.

links.label: Read the maximum declared object size

topics.title: Return the parsed byte count
topics.description: The count n becomes h$declared in the header handler. A decimal zero also returns zero and is rejected there, so admitted objects have a positive declared byte count.
links: Store and check the parsed count

topics.title: Reset header state for each response
topics.description: http_reply at priority 0 replaces pfd_headers with Headers(). Header counts, filename, declared length, bad and file count therefore start fresh for this response.

ranges.code:
event http_reply(c: connection, version: string, code: count, reason: string) &priority=0
{ c$http$pfd_headers=Headers(); }

topics.title: Inspect responder headers with HTTP state
topics.description: http_header at priority 0 returns for originator headers or a connection without HTTP state. h references this response pfd_headers for the following counters and quality flags.

topics.title: Require the outer response MIME depth
topics.description: A response MIME depth other than one marks the header state bad and returns. File admission checks depth again and requires a single outer response file.

topics.title: Bound each inspected response header value
topics.description: Any response header value above max_header_value_bytes marks h$bad and returns before name specific processing. The bound applies to all headers observed by this handler.

links.label: Read the shared header byte cap

topics.title: Select a Content-Disposition filename
topics.description: The exact event header name CONTENT-DISPOSITION increments cd_count and passes value to selected_filename. The actual parser returns the selected bytes into h$filename, including filename* precedence and an empty result for rejected syntax.

links.label: Follow filename selection at the actual parser definition

links: Use the selected name for file admission

topics.title: Parse one positive Content-Length
topics.description: CONTENT-LENGTH increments cl_count and stores decimal_length(value) into h$declared. A zero result sets bad, covering zero length, rejected syntax and a value exceeding the object cap.
links: Follow the actual decimal parser definition

topics.title: Require a complete unsegmented length profile
topics.description: TRANSFER-ENCODING and CONTENT-RANGE each mark the response bad. The accepted path uses one Content-Length and a complete response body for byte agreement.

topics.title: Accept at most one identity content encoding
topics.description: CONTENT-ENCODING increments ce_count. The stripped lowercased value must be identity and the count must be at most one, so the admitted body bytes use the identity representation.

ranges.code:
else if ( name=="CONTENT-ENCODING" )
{ ++h$ce_count; if ( to_lower(strip(value))!="identity" || h$ce_count>1 ) h$bad=T; }

topics.title: Require a single nonmultipart Content-Type when present
topics.description: CONTENT-TYPE increments ct_count. A value beginning with optional space or tab and multipart/ after lowercasing, or a repeated Content-Type, marks bad. An absent Content-Type leaves its count zero.

ranges.code:
else if ( name=="CONTENT-TYPE" )
{ ++h$ct_count; if ( /^[ \t]*multipart\// in to_lower(value) || h$ct_count>1 ) h$bad=T; }

topics.title: Reject repeated disposition or length fields
topics.description: More than one Content-Disposition or Content-Length marks h$bad after field handling. Even matching repeated values therefore fail admission.

topics.title: Admit only an outer HTTP responder file
topics.description: file_over_new_connection at priority 0 requires source HTTP, HTTP association, callback is_orig=F, a present native is_orig field that is F, and no parent_id. These predicates select the outer file carrying bytes from the HTTP responder.

topics.title: Count associated response files
topics.description: h references the file HTTP header state and files increments for each file reaching this point. Later admission and HTTP completion both require exactly one file.

topics.title: Reject a second association to a tracked response
topics.description: If the HTTP state already holds pfd_context, the handler rejects that shared context and returns. This prevents a later association from preserving an earlier single file finding.

topics.title: Require one complete HTTP 200 response association
topics.description: Admission requires good headers, one file, exactly one disposition and length, a nonempty selected name, status 200, no range_request and response MIME depth one. resp_fuids must exist, contain exactly one entry and identify this native file. These checks bind the advertised metadata to the one tracked response file.

topics.title: Require a listed document or image suffix
topics.description: The anchored suffix pattern on to_lower(h$filename) accepts the listed pdf, Office, OpenDocument and image extensions at the end of the selected bytes. The suffix is ASCII and case insensitive through lowercasing; earlier name checks supply the separate byte encoding and basename restrictions.

topics.title: Decline admission when context capacity is full
topics.description: When active_contexts reaches max_active_contexts, admission_drops increments and the handler returns before creating a context or adding an analyzer.

topics.title: Capture filename length and transaction identity
topics.description: The new Context copies c$uid, c$id, f$id, f$http$trans_depth, h$filename and h$declared. These values bind later parsing, completion and Notice arguments to this admitted response.
links: Read the stored name and length fields
Follow identity and metadata into sub

topics.title: Share the context with both native owners
topics.description: f$pfd_context and f$http$pfd_context reference the same x. The file and HTTP completion handlers therefore set independent flags and quality state on one shared context.
links: Set the HTTP flag on shared state
Set the file flag on shared state

topics.title: Account admitted context ownership
topics.description: active_contexts and eligible_files increment at admission. If this raises the simultaneous context peak, peak_active_contexts receives the new count. release_context later returns active ownership once.

topics.title: Attach only the prefix stream event instance
topics.description: Files::add_analyzer receives f, Files::ANALYZER_DATA_EVENT and [$stream_event=prefix_data]. Failure immediately rejects x. stop_prefix removes this exact argument instance after parsing or rejection.

topics.title: Retrieve context for streamed file bytes
topics.description: prefix_data receives a native file and the next data string. Files without pfd_context return immediately; otherwise x references the admitted shared state.

topics.title: Stop callbacks after release parse or failure
topics.description: A released, parsed or bad context calls stop_prefix and returns before retaining more bytes. This guard also covers stream callbacks already queued when the exact analyzer instance was detached.

ranges.code: if ( x$released || x$parsed || x$bad ) { stop_prefix(f); return; }

links: Remove the owned stream callback instance

topics.title: Consume each callback with a local cursor
topics.description: cursor starts zero for the current data string and the loop repeatedly recomputes the next required header extent. Several prefix stages can therefore be satisfied from one callback without appending its whole payload.

topics.title: Ask for the next necessary header extent
topics.description: needed(x$prefix) returns the next required prefix byte count using the bytes already retained. It stages DOS, signature plus COFF, then optional header and section table collection.

links.label: Follow the actual required prefix definition

topics.title: Bound the requested extent before copying
topics.description: A need above max_prefix_bytes or x$declared rejects the context and detaches the callback. Both the sentinel and an oversized computed table extent stop here.

ranges.code:
if ( need>max_prefix_bytes || need>x$declared )
{ reject_context(x); stop_prefix(f); return; }

topics.title: Classify when the required extent is present
topics.description: When the retained length reaches need, the following branch invokes pe_format once. Otherwise the cursor path copies only bytes still required by this stage.

topics.title: Store the PE result and stop prefix collection
topics.description: pe_format receives x$prefix and x$declared; its result becomes x$format and parsed becomes T. An empty result rejects x, while a recognized format releases only prefix bytes so completion can still qualify the context. stop_prefix detaches this callback in either case.

links.label: Follow the actual PE classifier definition

links: Release only bytes for an accepted format

topics.title: Wait for another callback when input is exhausted
topics.description: If cursor has consumed the complete data string before the required extent is present, the handler returns with the existing bounded prefix retained. A future callback restarts a cursor on new data.

topics.title: Select the smaller remaining span
topics.description: remaining is need minus retained prefix length and available is the unconsumed callback length. take is their minimum, bounding each append to the current stage and current callback.

topics.title: Append only the selected callback span
topics.description: part(data,cursor,take) supplies exactly the next span, cat appends it to x$prefix and cursor advances by take. The loop can now request the next stage from the newly available header fields.

links.label: Follow the zero based slice definition

topics.title: Account each retained byte and peak
topics.description: take is added to retained_prefix_bytes and may update peak_retained_prefix_bytes. release_prefix subtracts the retained string length when parsing ends or context cleanup occurs.

topics.title: Select the responder HTTP completion context
topics.description: http_message_done at priority 0 ignores originator completion and missing HTTP or context state. x refers to the admitted response context.

topics.title: Record the HTTP completion gate
topics.description: x$http_done becomes T independently of native file removal. finish still waits for file_done on an otherwise eligible context.
links: Wait for the other completion flag

topics.title: Require complete HTTP bytes and the same transaction
topics.description: An interruption, content gap, body length unequal to declared, changed transaction depth or UID, multiple response files or bad final headers sets x$bad. These checks qualify the completed response, including metadata changes after file admission.

ranges.code:
if ( stat$interrupted || stat$content_gap_length!=0 || stat$body_length!=x$declared ||
c$http$trans_depth!=x$depth || c$uid!=x$uid || c$http$pfd_headers$files!=1 || c$http$pfd_headers$bad ) x$bad=T;

topics.title: Evaluate completion after HTTP quality checks
topics.description: finish receives the shared context after the HTTP flag and quality state are updated. It either waits for file completion, rejects bad state or makes the final Notice decision.

topics.title: Retrieve state at native file removal
topics.description: file_state_remove at priority 0 returns for files without a context and otherwise retrieves the same x used by HTTP completion.

topics.title: Record completion and native observed counts
topics.description: file_done becomes T and seen receives f$seen_bytes. total receives f$total_bytes only when present; otherwise bad becomes T. completion_ok requires both native counts to equal the declared HTTP byte count.

ranges.code:
x$file_done=T; x$seen=f$seen_bytes;
if ( f?$total_bytes ) x$total=f$total_bytes; else x$bad=T;

links.label: Check both native counts against declared bytes

topics.title: Require a complete parsed native file
topics.description: Any missing bytes, overflow bytes, timed out file info or unset parsed flag sets bad. The finding path therefore requires complete native file evidence and a completed prefix parse.

ranges.code: if ( f$missing_bytes!=0 || f$overflow_bytes!=0 || f$info$timedout || ! x$parsed ) x$bad=T;

topics.title: Evaluate completion after native file checks
topics.description: finish receives x after native flags and counts have been recorded. Either callback order reaches the same both completion and exact count predicate.

ranges.before: if ( f$missing_bytes!=0 || f$overflow_bytes!=0 || f$info$timedout || ! x$parsed ) x$bad=T;

topics.title: Reject a file gap immediately
topics.description: file_gap rejects the attached context when one exists. Immediate cleanup releases its prefix and context budgets even if a completion callback has not arrived.

ranges.code:
event file_gap(f: fa_file, offset: count, len: count)
{ if ( f?$pfd_context ) reject_context(f$pfd_context); }

topics.title: Reject reassembly overflow immediately
topics.description: file_reassembly_overflow rejects any attached context. This converges on the same idempotent release used by prefix and completion failures.

ranges.code:
event file_reassembly_overflow(f: fa_file, offset: count, skipped: count)
{ if ( f?$pfd_context ) reject_context(f$pfd_context); }

topics.title: Reject a native file timeout immediately
topics.description: file_timeout at priority 0 rejects an attached context. Later queued events see released state and cannot reopen a finding.

ranges.code:
event file_timeout(f: fa_file) &priority=0
{ if ( f?$pfd_context ) reject_context(f$pfd_context); }

msg: PE content advertised with a document or image filename
